We can apply the distributive law

$$
AC+BC=(A+B)C.
$$

So, we calculate $A+B$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & -3 \\ -3 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AC+BC & =(A+B)C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].[\begin{aligned}-2 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
